benchmarks: SkillsBench (88 tasks; 38 filtered task-model pairs with oracle skills; library sizes |S| in {S*,52,102,202})
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Skill shadowing': as a skill library grows, distractor skills with superficially-matching descriptions displace the correct oracle skill during selection (up to 68% of the pass-rate drop, the only statistically-significant component, CI excludes zero at |S|=202); a smaller, statistically-indistinguishable-from-zero 'context overhead' effect also exists (enlarged context degrades execution even when selection is correct). No mitigation is implemented (pure diagnostic paper); Discussion proposes retrieval-based pre-filtering, description disambiguation, and learned routing as future fixes.
cita: Song and Wei (2026). More Skills, Worse Agents? Skill Shadowing Degrades Performance When Expanding Skill Libraries.
notes: Pure diagnostic/measurement paper over EXISTING full-context skill libraries (industry Agent-Skills convention, Anthropic/OpenAI SKILL.md): the agent context is simply q+D(S) = the FULL set of all skill (name,description) pairs injected at once, no retrieval/write/consolidation mechanism of its own is proposed -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA (mirrors the pure-measurement precedent: paper studies an existing paradigm, not its own architecture). S3 exact decomposition (Eq.10): library-induced pass-rate drop Delta(q,S)=p(q,S*(q))-p(q,S) splits into Delta_ctx(context overhead, event-probabilities fixed, only conditional pass-rates vary) + Delta_shd(skill shadowing, conditional pass-rates fixed, only selection-event probabilities vary), with derived upper bounds (Lemma1/2). This decomposition IS a precision/utility measurement of skill SELECTION (reading) as scale grows -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (rule3). Table1 (38 task-model pairs, 2545 trajectories, 95% two-stage clustered-bootstrap CI): at |S|=202, Delta_shd=.14[.06,.26] (CI excludes zero, dominant) vs Delta_ctx=.07[-.13,.25] (never separates from zero at any scale). Table2: event-o ('oracle only') trajectory share collapses from 88.0%(S*) to 52.6%(|S|=202), mass migrating into n('no skill', 12.0%->38.5%) and m('mixed/wrong skill', 0%->8.9%) -- two distinguishable failure sub-modes: abandonment and wrong selection. Table3 (mario-coin-counting example, Intro+AppendixA.4): a distractor 'video-frame-extraction' skill (superficially better textual match) shadows the correct oracle skill in ALL 26/26 trajectories -> CUALITATIVA anchor. Overall pass rate drops up to 21% (avg both models) at |S|=202; skill shadowing is the primary bottleneck, NOT the enlarged context -> NEGATIVO sense(b) (negative evidence against the assumed 'more skills=better' premise of skill-library scaling). F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO.

benchmarks: AFTER (own, 382 tasks, 6 professional roles, 22 procedural skills)
fallos_mitigaciones: Skills evolved from NARROW experience (single source context) exhibit 'source-context overfitting': specificity (train gain) improves while generality (test gain) degrades (Fig1 landscape). Mitigated by evolving from DIVERSE multi-task/role/model trace pools, which moves skills toward the desired high-specificity+high-generality regime (Table3: diverse evolution reaches +7.3 test-gain on pdf/xlsx/pptx vs narrow's often-negative test deltas). Separately, cross-role transfer is an unmitigated limitation: skills specialized to one role's workflow LOSE effectiveness (-4.8 to -7.5pp) when applied to a different role's use of the same nominal skill (Fig5, pdf skill PM<->DS).
cita: Belikova et al. (2026). Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: Control, Adaptation, and Evaluation.
notes: S2/S3: 22 skills as versioned SKILL.md artifacts (YAML+markdown, Agent-Skills format) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL; 'skill annotations are fixed at task definition rather than retrieved at solve time, separating skill quality from retrieval quality' -> retrieval=NA (retrieval explicitly out of scope by design). EVOLUTION harness: full-skill updates via COLLECT-DIAGNOSE-REVISE-PROMOTE cycle, s(v+1)=U_rho(s(v),Dsrc); rho='reflector' (model/procedure that inspects traces and PROPOSES revision, trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM) fires after each refinement round (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA pipeline stage) -> operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION; PROMOTE step + 'validation, promotion, rollback, and lineage tracking' -> ADMISION + fidelidad_procedencia=SI (explicit lineage/rollback/validation infrastructure). Diverse-trace evolution (n=5) aggregates multi-model/task traces into ONE updated skill -> CONSOLIDACION. S4.1 static valuation (Table2): comparing no-skill(NA) vs handcrafted(H) vs LLM-generated(G) skill CONTENT injected in-prompt directly measures content-utility (no retrieval step, since skills are fixed by design) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (the facet covers read-utility broadly, not only vector retrieval). Skills improve M2 by +2.8pts avg; single refinement round adds +5.2pts (S4.2, Fig3: +3.7 to +6.7 aggregate across model scales). S4.4 cross-model transfer (Fig4): diverse-source-evolved skills reach 73.1% test accuracy vs best single-source 59.4% (+13.7pp) -- weaker source models give BETTER transfer signal, a genuinely negative/counterintuitive finding (NEGATIVO sense b). Token efficiency (Fig6): evolved skills cut total tokens by 326k(62%, Claude)/48k(16%, Hermes) on Kafka-Lag-Anomaly-Detection -> COSTO-TOKENS. Spans SIX professional organizational roles (DE/DS/GenAI/Infra/PM/SWE) with explicit cross-ROLE transfer as a primary evaluation axis -> alcance=ORGANIZACION. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO, FIDELIDAD, CONSOLIDACION, COSTO.

benchmarks: own 7 authoring-domain benchmark suites (Web, Excel, Reaper, PPT, Blender, CAD, UE5; 80 task briefs/domain)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Directly placing raw videos into an agent's memory is expensive, redundant, and often impractical... compressing video into a plain text summary discards precisely the information that makes video useful: dynamic operations, before-after visual changes, animation quality, spatial layout, timing, tool interaction order.' Mitigated by the multimodal distiller fθ that extracts modality-specific evidence (key frames, code regions, prose passages, rendered exemplars) via a vision-capable LM and normalizes it into a structured (text,visual,code,metadata) entry instead of raw video or lossy text-only summarization, gated by a 5-check admission predicate (completeness, traceable provenance, deduplication, modality consistency, structural executability).
cita: Fan et al. (2026). Resource2Skills: Distilling Executable Skills from Human-Created Resources for Software Agents.
notes: S3.1 skill tuple s=(p,xtext,xvisual,xcode,m), p=taxonomy path, m=metadata for filtering/auditing/provenance -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL;MULTIMODAL, representacion=HIBRIDA (structured multimodal entries + hierarchical Skill Wiki). S3.2 construction operator fθ distills 4 resource families (video/code/article/artifact) into candidates, domain predicate A_D enforces 5 checks incl. 'traceable provenance' before acceptance (operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. S3.3 MetaBrowse: 2-stage selection, BM25 lexical scorer over name+tags+applicability+TAXONOMY-PATH narrows candidates (retrieval=RANKING;GRAFO, hierarchy directly favors topically-relevant subtrees), then an LM selects a SUBSET (can pick zero) to compose. S3.4 online acquisition reuses the SAME (fθ,A_D) operator when offline coverage is insufficient -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (coverage-gap condition). Table1 main comparison (4 backends x 4 systems x 7 domains, N=80/domain): w-Skills beats w/o-Skills in ALL 28 cells (56.8% vs 45.0%, +11.9pp) and beats the stronger off-the-shelf harness in 26/28 cells (paired Wilcoxon p<1e-3 in every GPT-5.4/5.5 cell); largest gains on UE5 (+30 to +40pp). Table2: offline-only vs offline+online acquisition: on Tstandard online adds only +0.7pp(noise), but on Tnovel(capability-gap stress test) online lifts 41.2%->62.8% (+21.6pp) -> pure gap-filler, not a booster. S4.4.1 panel-b ablation: Flat(pure-text list) vs Our-Wiki(hierarchical+multimodal) -- Wiki beats Flat by 2.5-8.2pp -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table3 source-ablation: holding Video out drops avg 68.9%->59.4% (video is the non-substitutable source, Excel -12.1pp/Web -9.8pp). Table4 matched-budget representation ablation isolates content-type value: Text-only=65.0%, +Visual=+1.9pp, +Code=+2.0pp, Full=68.9% (multimodal content itself adds gain beyond curated-text-memory alone). Blinded human A/B (200 paired ratings, 5 raters, 40 pairs x 7 domains, AppendixK, CUALITATIVA): w-Skills wins 83.3% of non-tied pairs. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

benchmarks: Spider 2.0 / Spider 2.0 Lite (547 enterprise Text-to-SQL tasks)
fallos_mitigaciones: Three explicit failure modes of memoryless agentic Text-to-SQL: (1) 'Repeated exploration' -- agents retrace identical schema-exploration steps across queries on the same database (fewer than 10-20% of trajectories are distinct per cited prior work), inflating cost/latency; mitigated by trajectory reuse via the Trajectory Store. (2) 'Strategy selection' -- a single rigid pipeline strategy fails on out-of-distribution queries (e.g. vector search invoked in only 30% of firebase questions when unnecessary, Fig2); mitigated by per-query dynamic trajectory retrieval instead of a fixed one-size-fits-all routine. (3) 'Reducing variance' -- small syntax deviations derail reasoning and cause inconsistent results even at temperature=0; mitigated by composite tools shortening trajectories. A further explicit negative finding (Table1): reading RAW/unstructured ('Naive') trajectories yields NO improvement over no trajectory at all (both 25% accuracy) -- structured Markdown/JSON representation is required to realize any gain (50% accuracy).
cita: Biswal et al. (2026). AgentSM: Semantic Memory for Agentic Text-to-SQL.
notes: S3.2 offline Trajectory Synthesis (Algorithm1): LLM-generated synthetic exploration-rich questions per database schema -> agent executes them -> raw trajectories are STEP-CLASSIFIED (regex-based intent matching into exploration/execution/validation phases, not position-based) and restructured into markdown with LLM-generated semantic headers (operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, mem_tipos=EPISODICA(trace-derived)+PROCEDIMENTAL(structured reusable 'programs')). Trajectory selection (Eq1-3): filter to same-database trajectories, then pick highest-semantic-similarity match to the current question -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS, representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (markdown/JSON trajectory files in a Trajectory Store). Table1 (20-question sample): 'No trajectory'/'Naive'(raw unstructured) BOTH give 25% accuracy/22.62 avg-steps identically -- raw-trajectory reading is USELESS; 'Markdown'/'JSON'(structured) reach 50% accuracy at 15-16.5 avg-steps -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (direct precision test of representation format on read-utility). Table2 main results (547-task Spider2.0-Lite): AgentSM reaches SOTA 44.8% overall accuracy, +14.1% over agentic baseline SpiderAgent, +20% over a plain CodingAgent. Table3 ablation (75-question sample): removing trajectory reading OR composite tools each sharply cuts accuracy while INCREASING token usage and latency; full method reduces avg trajectory length 25% and improves accuracy 35% vs no-trajectory-reading -> COSTO-TOKENS;ITERACION;LATENCIA. Two agents (planner + schema-linking) exist but explicitly do NOT share the trajectory-memory system: 'introducing additional agents would necessitate a shared memory... which we leave as future work' -> multiagente=NO; design DELIBERATELY avoids inter-agent handoff/control-transfer to prevent 'context loss commonly observed when control is handed off to specialized sub-agents' -> handoff=NO. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds WRITE, COSTO.

fallos_mitigaciones: Three fundamental obstacles to reusable procedural memory motivate the design: C1 Executability (episodic narratives are passive, not directly-instantiable procedures) -- addressed by the Skill-MDP's explicit <Activation,Procedure,Termination> structure; C2 Reusability (stored procedures must reliably transfer) and C3 Non-Parametric Optimization (must improve without weight updates while avoiding catastrophic forgetting/over-specialization) -- addressed jointly by the PPO Gate, which explicitly guards against candidates that 'extrapolate beyond the observed interaction data and introduce hallucinated or behaviorally unstable Skills' via trust-region verification (only admits ω' if J(ω')>0). Unbounded pool growth/redundancy is mitigated by online-score-based pruning: skills with non-positive score or duplicate/redundant skills are removed, 'phasing out obsolete Skills while retaining those with consistently positive gains.'
cita: Mi et al. (2026). Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents.
notes: S3.2 Skill omega=<I_omega,pi_omega,beta_omega> (activation/execution/termination), explicit natural-language readable form (representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL, contrasted throughout vs EPISODIC memory as the paper's central framing, Fig1). S4.1 Semantic Gradients: per-trajectory hindsight attribution -> batch-aggregated update direction -> candidate omega'=omega XOR g_omega (WRITE). S4.2 PPO Gate: importance-ratio+clipped-advantage verification (Eq6, LCLIP) admits only J(omega')>0 candidates (ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION). S4.3 online score+pruning removes non-positive-score/duplicate skills under fixed capacity K (OLVIDO, trigger=PRESUPUESTO); evolution operator E applied per-trajectory-batch (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA). Skill selection: Sim(st,I_omega) via cosine-embeddings-or-LLM-judge (retrieval=EMBEDDINGS) then top-k re-ranked by estimated Q-value (retrieval=RANKING). Table1 headline metric IS 'Experience Reuse Rate' (in-domain/cross-task/cross-agent) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO directly measures read-precision. Cross-agent: skills LEARNED on Gemma-2-9B are REUSED by Gemma-3-4B/Qwen3-32B/LLaMA-3.3-70B, a headline result -> multiagente=SI, handoff=CONTENIDO (the natural-language skill content itself travels between different agent backbones). Table1 efficiency: Skill-Pro stores only 816 tokens total vs baselines' 40510-391706 tokens (RAG/Expel/A-MEM/AWM/G-Memory) -> extreme memory compression -> COSTO-TOKENS; 'Retrieval Ratio' = probability of retrieving memory per step -> OTRA. Ablation (Table3/Fig3): Semantic-Gradients and PPO-Gate both indispensable; online-scoring preserves long-term evolutionary gains. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;MULTIAGENTE) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, WRITE, COSTO.

benchmarks: HumanEval-Hard (45 tasks), MBPP-Hard (117 tasks), via EvalPlus
fallos_mitigaciones: Existing first-order textual optimizers (TextGrad) are stateless: 'each optimization run begins tabula rasa,' causing inefficient zig-zagging/oscillation and excessive token consumption -- mitigated by the Hessian-Proxy Case Base of historical error-operator pairs. Separately, existing memory-augmented optimizers (REMO) retrieve by INPUT/problem similarity, which causes 'surface-level case overfitting' and fails to transfer across domains: Table3 shows MBPP-with-HumanEval-CB Plus-pass-rate COLLAPSES to 58.12%, barely above the 48.72% no-CB floor (a -20.51pp degradation vs in-domain retrieval) -- mitigated by TextBFGS's gradient/error-based retrieval instead, which maintains 74.36% Plus-pass-rate cross-domain (+16.24pp over REMO, Table4).
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval.
notes: S3.3 Hessian-Proxy Case Base M={(g_i,O_i)}: g_i=textual error/gradient (episodic, trace-derived), O_i=abstract adaptation operator (procedural rule) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;PROCEDIMENTAL; stored in ChromaDB indexed by Qwen3-Embedding-8B embeddings, top-k cosine retrieval on the QUERY gradient g_t^query=g_{t-1} ('Semantic Momentum', Eq6) -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. S3.5 Case Retention (operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION): only upon f(x_{t+1})>f(x_t) is the tuple (g_t,O_t) injected back into M (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA), enabling self-evolution. Case Base bootstrapped via TextBFGS(w/o CB) over 3 epochs -> 39 cases(HumanEval)/245 cases(MBPP), k=3 retrieved per query (matched to TextGrad-Momentum's 3-record window for fair comparison). S4.2 ablation (Table1/2): TextGrad(91.11/82.22% HumanEval Base/Plus) -> +Momentum(86.67% Plus) -> +CaseBase(TextBFGS-REMO 91.11%, TextBFGS 93.33% Plus) -- Case-Base integration is the single largest lever (+6.66pp over Momentum on HumanEval, +20.51pp on MBPP-Plus). S4.3 (Table3/4, the paper's central experiment) directly compares problem-based(REMO) vs error/gradient-based(TextBFGS) retrieval strategies IN-domain vs CROSS-domain -> this IS a rigorous mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO test: TextBFGS-REMO overfits to surface content (near-identical In-Domain 97.56% but collapses Cross-Domain to 58.12%), while TextBFGS's error-dynamics retrieval transfers robustly (96.34% In vs 93.33%/74.36% Cross) -- proves 'optimization logic...is more transferable than specific code instances.' S4.4: One-Pass fusion (gradient+operator+update in ONE LLM call) cuts token counts by -50.6%(HumanEval) with fewer model calls vs multi-step TextGrad pipelines -> COSTO-TOKENS;ITERACION. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds COSTO.
